quarterly_data.signal: Q4 and full-year 2025 results (CEO): Q4 revenues were $3.33 billion, above the midpoint of the business outlook range, driven by Personal Electronics and to a lesser extent Communication Equipment and Computer Peripheral and Industrial, while Automotive was below expectations; gross margin of 35.2% was above the midpoint, mainly on better product mix; diluted EPS excluding impairment, restructuring and phaseout costs was $0.11, including negative one-time tax expenses of $0.18 per share. Q4 revenue 'marked the return to year-over-year growth'; inventories were worked down on the balance sheet and in distribution; Q4 free cash flow was $257 million. Full year 2025: net revenues decreased 11.1% to $11.8 billion (strong decrease in Automotive, lesser in Industrial; Personal Electronics and Communication Equipment and Computer Peripheral both grew); gross margin 33.9%, down from 39.3% in 2024; net CapEx $1.79 billion; free cash flow $265 million. CFO: 2025 revenue by end market was Automotive about 39%, Personal Electronics about 25%, Industrial about 21% and Communication and Computer Peripheral about 15%; OEM 72% and distribution 28%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenues $3.33 billion; gross margin 35.2%; non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.11; Q4 free cash flow $257 million; FY2025 net revenues $11.8 billion (decreased 11.1%); FY gross margin 33.9% vs 39.3%; FY net CapEx $1.79 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 segment detail (CFO): year-over-year, Analog products, MEMS and sensor grew 7.5% (mainly Imaging), Power and Discrete products decreased by 31.6%, Embedded Processing was up 1% to 2%, and RF and optical communication grew 22.9%; sequentially, RF and optical communication was up 30.5% while Power and Discrete was the only segment to decrease (by 3.9%). Q4 non-GAAP operating margins: Analog/MEMS/Sensor 16.2%, Power and Discrete negative 30.2%, Embedded Processing 19.2%, RF and Optical Communication 23.4%. Communication equipment and computer peripherals were up 23% sequentially (the CFO's year-over-year end-market breakdown said communication equipment and computer peripheral and personal electronics 'both grew by about 17%', which differs from the CEO's 22% below); CEO: 'our CCP segment grew sequentially 23% and year-over-year 22%', linked to the low-earth-orbit satellite business and driven by both its first customer and the second one ('it's significant'). The LEO business, based on ST's BiCMOS and panel level packaging technologies, saw shipments ramping to its second largest customer; ST is expanding its LEO customer base and expects continued revenue growth as constellations expand into applications such as direct-to-cell.
quarterly_data.figure: Power and Discrete decreased by 31.6% YoY, operating margin negative 30.2%; RF and optical communication grew 22.9% YoY and 30.5% sequentially, operating margin 23.4%; CCP up 23% sequentially and 22% YoY per CEO (CFO end-market breakdown: grew by about 17% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 2026 outlook (CEO): revenues of $3.04 billion, a decrease of 8.7% sequentially, plus or minus 350 basis points; gross margin about 33.7%, plus or minus 200 basis points, including about 220 basis points of unused capacity charges; no impact assumed from further changes to global tariffs. CFO: Q1 net OpEx about $860 million; the Q1 gross margin is 'clearly the lowest point in the year', with a mild increase in Q2 and a more significant increase in H2 as unloading charges keep falling; Q4 2026 gross margin is expected to be better than Q4 2025; FY2026 net OpEx expected at a low single-digit increase; Q1 inventory expected in the range of 140 days (130 days at year-end). CEO (no full-year guide): confident in the ability to grow organically in 2026; Q2 seasonality is 'low mid-single digit' and 'we absolutely see no reason that we will not be at least capable to deliver it'; in Q1 the embedded processing segment will grow 'above 30% year-over-year', led by general-purpose microcontrollers.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 revenues $3.04 billion (decrease of 8.7% sequentially); gross margin about 33.7% including about 220 basis points of unused capacity charges; Q1 net OpEx about $860 million

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 capex plan (CEO): 'In terms of net CapEx for 2026, we plan to invest about $2.2 billion to support capacity addition for selected growth drivers like those for cloud optical interconnect and our manufacturing reshaping plan' (2025 net CapEx was $1.79 billion, lower than the $2.5 billion of 2024).

AI data-center revenue ambition as of this call (later raised): in communication equipment, computer peripheral and data centers, 'including cloud, optical interconnect and power and analog for AI servers and data centers, with the current market dynamic, we believe we can deliver $1 billion revenue before 2030 with already USD 500 million in 2026.' The 2026 driver is cloud optical interconnect - photonics ICs, analog mixed-signal ICs and high-performance general-purpose microcontrollers - because 'the connectivity engine of the server will move to optical one.' In Q4 ST continued to work with customers to bring its silicon photonics technology to market, and optical-connectivity momentum 'contributed to a significant rise in demand for our high-performance microcontroller used in pluggable optics.'
quarterly_data.figure: $1 billion revenue before 2030; USD 500 million in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: AI data-center power (CEO): in Q4 ST secured multiple design wins for silicon and silicon carbide-based power solutions supporting next-generation AI compute architectures. On data-center power devices ST said it was 'a bit delay' and is in 'process to close the gap and offer solution to our customers'; in 2026 'we will start to contribute to the power supply unit' and to server power delivery, while the cloud optical interconnect remains the main data-center growth engine.

Silicon carbide and manufacturing reshaping: after a significant contraction in 2025, ST anticipates SiC power-device revenue returning to growth in 2026 and recovering to 2024 levels by 2027; CEO: 'up to now in Q1, we have a good book-to-bill on silicon carbide that is very encouraging.' Asked by an analyst about the Sanan partnership, the CEO said 'we will start to ramp up the facilities now' and that it 'will be a key success factor in our capability to compete on the Chinese market.' CFO: the reshaping program is progressively reducing 150-millimeter silicon carbide and 200-millimeter silicon capacity and moving product to 8-inch silicon carbide and 300-millimeter silicon - the main reason unused capacity charges decline in Q1; Q4 gross margin included about 50 basis points of nonrecurring reshaping cost, with a similar impact expected in the next few quarters; manufacturing-efficiency benefits are expected toward the second part of 2027 and 2028, and the program is on track.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 gross margin included about 50 basis points of nonrecurring reshaping cost; SiC revenue to recover to 2024 levels by 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and channel (CEO): Industrial book-to-bill was 'well above parity' and POS was growing 'between low teens, mid-teens', with distribution inventory normalizing; Q4 Industrial revenues rose 5% sequentially and 5% year-over-year. Automotive book-to-bill, corrected for a few key customers that place six-month orders in one shot, was parity; Q4 Automotive grew 3% sequentially but was below expectations on lower inventory pulls by some Tier 1s and soft legacy applications. Excess inventory expected to be cleared by end of Q2 2026, so ST will be exposed directly to end demand in H2. Company-specific 2026 drivers: ADAS ASICs, the NXP MEMS sensor acquisition (still expected to close in H1 2026), general-purpose MCUs on track to return to the historical market share of about 23% by 2027, and higher silicon content at its main Personal Electronics customer (no significant memory-price impact detected).
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial book-to-bill well above parity; Automotive book-to-bill parity; Q4 Industrial up 5% sequentially and 5% YoY; GP MCU market share target about 23% by 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Edge / physical AI (CEO): at the November STM32 Summit ST announced the first microcontroller built on the 18-nanometer process, next-generation wireless microcontrollers and an updated suite of edge AI software tools. ST says it is uniquely positioned in robotics (printed as 'human wind robotics') through MCUs, MEMS, optical sensors, GNSS and power management, is 'already generating revenues through engagements with major OEMs', and estimates its current addressable bill of material at about $600 per system.
quarterly_data.figure: addressable bill of material about $600 per system
